question: is there published data on the heat a standard air-cooled 911 head sees, to replace the declared boundary values of the assembly thermal screen
answer: No factory or peer-reviewed head temperature, heat balance or fan power for the 911 engine could be opened. What is citable is generic: head temperature limits, an effective gas temperature measured on 1930s aircraft cylinders, chamber and port heat loadings, exhaust gas and valve temperatures, and an upper bound of the air-side coefficient. They bound the declared case; none calibrates it.
not_found: a factory head temperature limit or operating value for the 911
an SAE, MTZ or ATZ paper with measured 911 head temperatures
a heat balance of the 911 engine, or its heat to oil
fan power, and the share of the cooling air that reaches the heads
contact conductance at a valve seat or at the cylinder joint as a number
a single published chamber heat transfer coefficient (the correlations need a cylinder pressure trace)
